articles.title: Claude Code sends your email address to websites
articles.summary: Claude Code sends your email address to websites

top_comments: Biggest questions here, which I think need answering:Should Claude have access to user details? I’d say no, unless explicitly entered manually into a chat.Should Claude have access to anything outside of the sandboxed project files without explicit permission? I’d again say no.Should Claude have internet access without a clear log of all requests made?Instances of Claude should be heavily sandboxed and kept away from user data, far more so than they are now. The impression given by the desktop UI is that the LLM only has access to things explicitly added to a project.This impression is not true, as evidenced by Claude pulling data from other sessions outside a project even when not instructed to (I’ve seen this a few times), and in this case pulling your email (from account details, user contacts? I wonder where it got that info?).None of this information should be available to Claude, by design, not by instruction. Using text instructions to try to limit these machines is an incredibly flawed approach and should not be necessary for important info. Anthropic should have the model access completely locked down by controls at the os level over file access, not open by default. That is how to fix this.If a user wants to open access that should be an explicit choice from them, with a warning about possible consequences.

Many people report seeing this behavior when using the SEC API specifically which makes me think that service is requesting this. Maybe email is required by the SEC API?---UPDATE: The SEC API documentation requires your email in the User-Agent and will reject you otherwise. Demo: U='https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyconcept/CIK0000320193/us-gaap/Assets.json' curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'response: %{http_code} curl default User-Agent, rejected\n' "$U" curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'response: %{http_code} email in user-agent, success\n' -A 'Acme Research admin@acme-research.example' "$U" response: 403 curl default, rejected response: 200 email in user-agent, success SEC docs: https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-search-assistance/a...So basically Claude is trying to problem solve, and just does what the SEC asks. It's a 'prompt injection attack', but the entity instructing this behavior is the SEC. Tricky alignment problem. Pretty silly mechanism, since of course there's no email validation. (edit: turns out the SEC will accept most any non-cURL user-agent, email not actually required)

The amount of newsroom jobs fell 60% between 2008 and 2020. The vast majority of what was lost were "beat" reporters - foreign bureaus, Washington bureaus from regional publications, statehouse reporters, or regional specialty beats (science, law, etc).This started long before the decline of the open internet and AI. If anything, the shift online covered up a massive hollowing out of the industry. We're getting fewer sources of news, and more national coverage. A lot of stuff that is reported on is coming from a scant number of wire services, or directly from PR teams themselves.For the most part, your choice of news platform is just a layer of coverage choices and political spin on top of a very thin market of original coverage.
This article didn't generate any comments when it made the rounds 10 years ago. An obituary for what salon.com used to be.https://web.archive.org/web/20210219012551/https://www.polit...

I operate an online publication that has been online for an amount of time that can be accurately described as "decades," though not quite as long as Salon.My project had a brief window of modest profitability from about 2012 to 2020. Before and after that time, I've mostly operated at a break-even or a loss because I love doing it, and it gives me a sense of purpose, and the thought of packing it up is deeply depressing. But the past few years have been an extreme drought of donations, which leads to extreme drought in ambition and energy. I sometimes wonder if my mental health would improve if I turned out the lights and moved on to something else. I don't want to, but sometimes we humans fail to want what's good for us.I'm sure it doesn't help that I reject advertising and rely solely on donations. But perhaps the only thing more depressing than shutting down is slapping ads on everything. Blah.
